content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"Both queues are getting far more calls than forecast. General is running +25-43% since 09:30 (+34% in the alert), and payments climbed from +2% to +25% by 10:45. Staffing is close to plan: absences are normal (2 logged vs about 2.5 usual per queue) and agents on phones are within 1-2 of plan. AHT is at or below forecast, so this is not system slowness. There are no incidents and no marketing entries. In general, the rise is spread evenly across every reason (ratios 1.17-1.39), and in payments it is broad too, with card_declined (1.40) and payment_status_enquiry (1.29) only somewhat higher. Nothing points to a single root cause, so this is an unexplained demand surge. Service level fell to 17.8% on payments and 50.5% on general at 10:45.","plan_name":"Dual-queue surge response: borrow, add and deflect capacity","rationale":"Both queues are well below 70% service level, so neither can donate agents and cross-skill moves are ruled out. Based on the 10:45 interval, payments needs about 48 agents against 39 on phones, and general about 47 against 35, so roughly 9-12 extra agents each. Planned steps: (1) Delay breaks on both queues by 30 minutes, which is free and covers the gap until overtime arrives. (2) Cancel non-mandatory coaching until 14:00. (3) Run consecutive 2-hour overtime offers on both queues from 11:30 to 15:30. At about 40% acceptance this is roughly 16 accepted agents over 2-hour blocks, costing about Rs 11,700, within the Rs 15,000 budget. (4) Deflect eligible simple enquiries to chat at a 0.2 share, costing about Rs 4,100. (5) Offer callbacks to long-wait callers to shave peak load. This is a mixed set of levers because the gap is large and broad. No outage message is used because no outage is
